patch_description: The current algorithm computes a single Dijkstra shortest path from src to each dst and assigns ALL partitions of that dst to the same path. This (1) overloads a single route with all num_partitions flows, and (2) ignores network diversity. A better strategy is to compute k-shortest (lowest-cost) candidate paths per dst and spread partitions across those paths. To balance load across networks, we dynamically inflate the cost of edges as they get used (congestion-aware pricing): each time an edge carries a partition, its effective cost is increased multiplicatively, so subsequent paths tend to reuse different, less-utilized links. This exploits multi-network topologies, reduces redundant transfers over hot links, and spreads load, lowering overall cost and improving throughput feasibility. We use nx.shortest_simple_paths to get candidate paths in cost order, and assign partitions round-robin among the best candidates while tracking per-edge utilization.
